grok.summary: The signed D.110c-0c1f2 correction at 1502d4d81e1769a75bc3c416937b53e57dc3390b closes Kimi’s three P1s and the size stop without widening authority. A private digest-keyed (author, authorSequence) map, populated only after the existing exact preimage/digest/signature/anchor/epoch/object/ACL/admission checks and captured with non-anchor key-set/cardinality equality, is sufficient: close need not duplicate signature or preimage bytes, recoveries re-derive identity from those same verified preimages, and census/reclamation with the graph prevent stale or unbounded identity. Owners now cover capture, recovery, adoption (including authenticatedSuccessorIssuanceScope), close, transition, census, and reclamation without changing EpochVertex, public API, dependencies, thresholds, or the wire vertex. The application-writer vector is exactly authorizeLatchedApplicationWrite() for both permissionless (every member) and permissioned (writer-group) snapshots, including successor reopen; non-write-authorized ACL-operation authors get no frontier and fail closed. Aggregate 0→1 seeds the legacy-authenticated creator from v1, starts other writers at null/zero, refuses observed non-creator pre-aggregate gaps, and requires legacy/aggregate creator identity and frontier equality on every coexistence close, with a non-null aggregate entry as the selected capability. The canonical two-element [author, admittedAuthorSequence] tuple is one-to-one with the rejected object form, encodes the legal 64-entry maximum to 6,241 bytes (1,951 under the unchanged 8,192-byte ceiling), and GREEN must reproduce that exact size while rejecting every alternate shape. Fixed signed fields plus prior-aggregate adjacency still bind object, genesis, both ACLs, cut/QC/snapshot, and adjacent epochs under an independent signature domain. The two-layer tests-only RED still fails for the absent aggregate carrier on a genuine two-writer permissioned path, not because tuples or permissionless reopen are unimplemented. Ordinary cold reopen stays O(1) in epoch count and O(current authorized members). Pending/published custody, dense gaps, scan ceilings, two rollback generations, pruning, and runtime reclamation remain fail-closed. D.110c-c/d, archive, repeated-transition, and Phase-7 work stay separately owned. P2 dispositions are frozen and do not block RED.

kimi.summary: Material confirmation of the corrected D.110c-0c1f1/D.110c-0c1f2 plan at signed/pushed 1502d4d81e1769a75bc3c416937b53e57dc3390b against first reviewed plan 5e0170670973f4920731a6d418436c9b4ae971ff and closure anchor 244c935f9e715236e9f2c2783f3bb6bee24706e1. Custody verified: the correction commit carries a good GPG signature and is contained in the pushed origin branch; the 5e017067..1502d4d8 diff touches only the plan document and matches the hash-validated plan.diff exactly; both log manifests validate (16/16 and 5/5); all seven audited source files hash identically to source-hashes.txt, so the audit's seam facts still hold at the corrected tree. All three first-review P1s are closed exactly as their required_actions demanded. (1) The capture-side owner is now declared: the private digest-keyed (author, authorSequence) map extends the existing applicationVertices/applicationAuthors retention seam (v3-live.ts:1549, populated only from AuthenticatedRecoveryVertex at 4245 after the full canonical-preimage/digest/signature/anchor/epoch/object/ACL/admission pipeline), joins the existing census (2949-2965) and per-generation reclamation (3148), and captureCloseGraph (7297) already enforces exact cardinality. Digest binding of the admission-verified preimage makes duplicated signature/preimage bytes redundant; key-set/cardinality equality prevents substitution or omission; one entry per retained vertex bounded by maxEpochVertices prevents hidden growth. The shared compaction EpochVertex type, public handle, product API, and wire vertex are untouched. (2) The corrected writer-set rule matches authorizeLatchedApplicationWrite (latched-acl.ts:336) exactly - every member when permissionless, otherwise writer-group members - and permissionless writer-group operations are operation-invalid (401-403); the genuinely defective literal filter at creator-adoption.ts:876 is brought under the same owner for both close and successor reopen, and non-write-authorized ACL-operation authors receive no frontier and fail closed by design. (3) Aggregate 0-to-1 seeding is deterministic: the legacy-authenticated creator seeds at the v1 carrier's admittedAuthorSequence, other writers start at null and advance only from sequence zero, observed non-creator pre-aggregate gaps refuse with the exact migration token, per-close legacy/aggregate creator identity/frontier equality plus non-null-aggregate-selected precedence removes the dual-carrier ambiguity, and null-plus-nonzero lineage deterministically emits the reentry refusal. All three P2 dispositions are concretely owned; the maximum-shape overflow disposition executed exactly as frozen (0c1f1 stopped at 8,289 bytes, 97 over; no ceiling raise, no field omitted). The 0c1f2 tuple reslice retains every fixed signed field and changes only entry representation to exact two-element [author, admittedAuthorSequence] arrays; the canonical encoder supports arrays and rejects holes (canonical/src/index.ts:213-217), the opener canonical-roundtrip pattern enforces canonicity, and the 2,048-byte saving is exactly 64 entries of removed repeated-key overhead, yielding 6,241 bytes with 1,951 bytes of headroom under the unchanged 8,192-byte ceiling at the legal maximum shape (64-member ACL cap at latched-acl.ts:134), with GREEN required to reproduce the exact size through the real encoder and reject all alternate tuple/object shapes. The fixed preimage fields bind protocol/kind/version, object, pinned genesis, closed/successor epoch and anchor, both ACL digests, cut-value digest, commit-QC ref, snapshot-manifest digest, and the prior-aggregate chain or genesis sentinel - a superset of the v1 binding - preventing cross-object, genesis, ACL, cut, QC, snapshot, skipped-epoch, stale/fork replay, and signature-domain confusion (the new domain ts-drp/creator-author-issuance-frontiers/v1 is distinct; the reused signing-request custody is verified opaque one-use WeakMap digest custody). The two-layer RED still fails for the intended absent aggregate carrier with explicit noncausal-stop guards covering tuple-production absence, permissionless setup validity, and earlier fixture/recovery defects. Ordinary cold reopen remains O(1) in epoch count and O(current authorized members): one unique aggregate opened against the independently authenticated floor, one selected entry, the shared maxEpochVertices logical-scan ceiling, and no archive, bootstrap, registration, lifetime-author, or proof-chain dependency. Pending/published outbox custody, dense-gap boundary truncation, two rollback generations, pruning, and runtime reclamation remain fail closed. No necessary schema, API, dependency, authority, or threshold change is absent from the declared high-risk boundary; same-key re-entry transparency is explicitly deferred to a future separately reviewed prerequisite if golden paths require it. The blocking P0/P1 union is empty; causal RED is authorized under the corrected plan.

findings.title: The private admitted-identity map is not pinned to the existing `applicationAuthors` map, and a second parallel map would touch the frozen runtime census outside the declared owner list
findings.evidence: The plan freezes "a private bounded map alongside `applicationVertices`" holding "exactly its verified `author` and `authorSequence`", but does not say it is the map that already exists. `packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:2546` already declares `applicationAuthors: Map<string,string>`; `retainApplicationVertex()` (v3-live.ts:1549-1558) already writes `authenticated.author` for every admitted non-anchor vertex at the exact three populate sites the plan names — local issue (6016), received ingress (3883), journal recovery (5210, 5403) — from `AuthenticatedRecoveryVertex` (v3-live.ts:4245-4252), which already carries `authorSequence` and is only constructed after full admission verification. The map is already anchor-excluding (seeded empty at 5050 while vertices/charges are seeded from the payload), already released with the graph (3148), and already censused (2949, 2965, 2996). Extending its value in place needs no census change; adding a *second* map requires a new key in the exact-key `D109dRuntimeCensus` at `packages/node/src/internal/runtime-reclamation.ts:16-19`, a file that is not in the declared owner list.
findings.impact: Under the repo's exact-owner discipline (the same rule that forced the D.110c-0c1d stop-and-reslice over two out-of-owner predicates), an implementer who adds a parallel map instead of extending the existing one hits an out-of-owner census edit mid-GREEN and an exact-owner diff-gate failure. No RED risk, and the cheaper compliant option is available today.
findings.required_action: Owner: `v3-live.ts` admission-identity retention/copy/close capture. Disposition: state that the identity map is the existing `applicationAuthors` map with its value extended in place to `{author, authorSequence}` (updating the blueprint-fold consumer at v3-live.ts:6913 that currently reads the value as a `string`), so the frozen `D109dRuntimeCensus` key set and `internal/runtime-reclamation.ts` are unchanged. Dispose without recursive review.

findings.title: The legacy/aggregate creator-equality law has no branch for a successor ACL that de-authorizes the creator's application writes, which would brick close for a configuration that closes today
findings.evidence: The vector "must equal the successor snapshot's application-write-authorized member set exactly", and "On every close where both carriers exist, the aggregate creator entry and unique legacy v1 identity must authenticate the same author and exact admitted frontier; a missing or unequal pair is ambiguity and refuses before staging." The v1 carrier is mandatory at every close and always binds the close owner's own scope (`creator-close.ts:261-315`, throwing `CREATOR_ISSUANCE_RETIREMENT_UNAVAILABLE` when `identity.author !== input.issuanceScope.author`), and it still derives a boundary when the creator issued nothing new (`creator-issuance-retirement-boundary.ts:100,130`). `stageLatchedAclOperations` guards only `last-admin`, not last-writer, so an admin may revoke the creator's `writer` group in a permissioned room; `authorizeLatchedApplicationWrite` (latched-acl.ts:325-342) then excludes the creator from the vector while the legacy carrier still authenticates it.
findings.impact: After GREEN, such a room produces a permanent "missing pair" ambiguity at every close, and only the creator can close, so the room becomes unclosable. It is fail-closed, not unsafe, and it is off the Discord/MMORPG golden path (permissionless rooms include every member, and permissioned creators normally hold `writer`), but the plan's stated law silently converts a currently-working configuration into a brick.
findings.required_action: Owner: `creator-close.ts` graph/ACL frontier derivation. Disposition: state that the equality law applies only when the successor write-authorized set contains the legacy v1 author, and name the deterministic outcome (an explicit refusal token or an explicit exemption) when the successor ACL de-authorizes that author; add the corresponding mutant to the GREEN roster. Dispose without recursive review.

findings.title: The exact 6,241-byte maximum-shape assertion is not pinned to the objectId bound that governs it
findings.evidence: `size-probe.json` fixes the maximum shape at `objectIdCharacters: 256`, and GREEN "must reproduce that result through the real protocol encoder and assert the exact maximum-shape byte length". Two different object-ID bounds exist in source: protocol-v3 certifies object IDs up to 1,024 bytes (`packages/protocol-v3/src/index.ts:395` and `:732`), while the latched ACL restricts them to `/^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,256}$/` (`latched-acl.ts:4`). The carrier binds both ACL digests, so 256 ASCII characters is the true legal maximum, but the plan never says so. Under the frozen canonical codec the difference is exactly 768 bytes: a 1,024-character shape encodes to ~7,009 bytes, not 6,241.
findings.impact: A GREEN maximum-shape test built against the 1,024-byte certified bound asserts the wrong exact length and would trip the frozen "any drift above 8,192 bytes still stops and reslices" fallback for a non-defect. The ceiling itself is never at risk — 7,009 bytes still leaves 1,183 bytes of headroom — so this is an acceptance-criterion determinism gap, not a sizing failure.
findings.required_action: Owner: D.110c-0c1f2 plan owner plus the protocol encoder maximum-shape test. Disposition: state that the carrier's `objectId` is the ACL-bounded ≤256-character identity that the assertion uses, and record that the 1,024-byte certified bound still fits. Dispose without recursive review.

findings.title: Record-level legality of the aggregate's genesis sentinel is unpinned and cannot reuse the v1 predicate
findings.evidence: The preimage carries "prior aggregate candidate digest or a domain-separated genesis sentinel", and 0→1 initialization is legal at any `closedEpoch` because the plan's own GREEN gate requires "A separate legacy creator-only room seeds its first aggregate from the v1 carrier". The v1 record's validity predicate binds the sentinel to genesis only — `record.closedEpoch === 0 ? prior === null && priorDigest === GENESIS_SENTINEL : prior !== null && priorDigest !== GENESIS_SENTINEL` (`creator-issuance-retirement.ts:207-211`) — so it cannot be copied. The plan states the 0→1 rule only as a closure transition law, not as an opener predicate.
findings.impact: Copying the v1 predicate makes the legacy-room adoption path (an explicit GREEN gate) impossible; omitting it silently leaves the 0→1-only rule resting entirely on the transition-advance closure inspection. Both directions are fail-closed — a re-initialized aggregate can only lower frontiers, never elevate one above current-graph evidence, and the opener still binds the record to the authenticated current floor — so neither is a safety hole, but the contract is not yet exact at this seam.
findings.required_action: Owner: the new protocol-v3 carrier's record-validity predicate plus the `creator-transition-advance.ts` normalization. Disposition: state that the sentinel is record-legal at any `closedEpoch` and that 0→1 is enforced solely by the absence of a prior aggregate in the authenticated current closure; add a mutant proposing a sentinel-bearing aggregate while a prior aggregate is present. Dispose without recursive review.

opus.summary: Confirmed the corrected D.110c-0c1f1/0c1f2 plan at signed/pushed `1502d4d81e1769a75bc3c416937b53e57dc3390b` (good GPG signature, pushed ref, plan.diff touches only `docs/production-hardening/production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md`) against first-reviewed plan `5e017067` and closure anchor `244c935f`. The blocking union is empty; four P2s take concrete owners and dispositions. (1) The private digest-keyed `(author,authorSequence)` fact is sufficient: `applicationAuthors` (v3-live.ts:2546) already exists and is written only from `AuthenticatedRecoveryVertex` (4245-4252, already carrying `authorSequence`) after the full preimage/digest/signature/anchor/epoch/object/ACL/admission checks, at exactly the three populate sites the plan names (3883 ingress, 5210/5403 recovery, 6016 local issue); the frontier is an admission ceiling, and the reopening writer independently re-verifies its own bytes in `authenticatedCoveredHistoricalOutboxRow` (4660-4690), so duplicating signature/preimage bytes into close would add no authority. Key-set/cardinality equality is exactly checkable because `captureCloseGraph` already asserts `vertices.size === charges.size + 1` with the anchor deleted (7300-7302), and the map is already cleared with the graph (3148) and censused (2949/2965/2996) — no growth beyond `maxEpochVertices`, no lifetime-author state. (2) The owner list now covers every seam without a shared-type or public-API change: `EpochVertex` (compaction/types.ts:2-13) is untouched; `V3CreatorCloseRegistration` is a private duplicated interface (v3-live.ts:387, creator-close.ts:114), both declared owners; the reused signing request is generic over the digest (`mintCreatorIssuanceRetirementSigningRequest`/`consume…`, and keychain `signCreatorIssuanceRetirementRequest` at finality.ts:168-191 signs any consumed 32-byte digest), so the new domain needs no keychain or dependency change; no closure-candidate count ceiling exists (only per-candidate `MAX_SCANNABLE_BYTES`), so no threshold change. (3) The permissionless-aware set is exact and matches `authorizeLatchedApplicationWrite` (latched-acl.ts:325-342); the correction correctly pulls in `creator-adoption.ts:876`, which today uses the literal `groups.includes("writer")` filter and therefore fails permissionless reopen at `writers.length === 0`; non-write-authorized ACL-operation authors are explicitly frontier-less and fail closed. (4) Seeding, continuing derivation, dual-carrier equality, removal, rollback, quiescent legacy writers, and same-key re-entry are deterministic and fail closed; the mandatory per-close v1 carrier (creator-close.ts:261-315) makes coexistence the steady state, and the store-derived v1 boundary and graph-derived aggregate boundary agree in every reachable state (the store-side laws at boundary.ts:97,125,130 refuse first otherwise). The 0→1-refuses-migration vs continuing-leaves-null asymmetry is correct: refusing a continuing close would let a re-added author brick the room. (5) The tuple form is canonical and one-to-one under the frozen codec: arrays are length-prefixed and tag-distinct from objects/maps, sparse arrays are rejected at encode and impossible at decode, and re-encode equality plus positional type predicates reject swapped/short/long/object forms. I independently reproduced the probe arithmetic: object→tuple saves exactly 32 bytes/entry × 64 = 2,048, and 8,289 − 2,048 = 6,241, with my field-by-field reconstruction of the frozen preimage landing within one byte of 8,289; 64 is the real ceiling (`members.length > 64` at latched-acl.ts:134). (6) The fixed signed set mirrors the proven v1 record plus both ACL digests under a separate domain, with prior-aggregate adjacency and floor binding preventing cross-object/genesis/cut/QC/snapshot/fork/skipped-epoch replay. (7) RED stays causal: a two-writer close succeeds today and yields only the creator's v1 carrier, and the second writer's reopen fails at the intended foreign-author historical refusal because `scopeAuthorMatches`/`identity.author === issuanceScope.author` (4650-4659) reject it — not because tuple production is missing or permissionless setup is invalid, provided the RED room is permissioned, which the noncausal-stop guard enforces anyway. (8) Cold reopen stays O(1) in epochs and O(≤64 members) with no archive, bootstrap, registration, or proof-chain dependency. (9) Custody, dense gaps, the single combined `maxEpochVertices` logical-scan ceiling, two rollback generations, pruning, and runtime reclamation remain fail closed. (10) No necessary schema, API, dependency, authority, or threshold change is missing from the declared high-risk boundary. RED is authorized; the P2s belong to GREEN specification and need no further prose review.
